purpose: A decorative glyph in a tinted, solid or gradient shape that gives a card, empty state, dialog header or feature list a visual anchor. The text beside it carries the meaning.

notFor.case: An icon the person can press.

Default.meaning: Static; Variant and Appearance set the look.
Default.visual: soft: Surface/accent with Content/accent (default), Surface/muted with Content/secondary (secondary), Status/<severity>/surface with Status/<severity>/content; solid: Action/primary/default with Content/on-action, Surface/inverse with Content/inverse, Status/<severity>/surface-solid with Status/<severity>/on-solid; gradient: the solid role through its hover and pressed steps, with Elevation/highlight.

notes: Never the only carrier of meaning: the title or text beside it says what it means.

openQuestions: Gradient: Figma paints root.fill as a linear gradient, while the contract binds a solid role (Action/primary/default, Action/secondary/default, Status/<severity>/surface-solid). No gradient role exists. Should one be added? (findings PAR-001 FeaturedIcon root.fill)
Gradient in dark: the warning and info stops converge on pale tones. Should their stops change? (finding COL-003)
Gradient shadow: Figma paints no spread, the CSS has -1 and -2. Which is right? (finding SYN-009)
